name: Parietal cell (stomach acid cell)
short_description: Large plump pyramidal acid-secreting cell of the gastric glands: deeply invaginated intracellular secretory canaliculi lined with microvilli, an extreme density of mitochondria (about a third of cell volume) powering H+/K+-ATPase proton pumps that acidify the stomach to pH 1; also the source of intrinsic factor for vitamin B12 uptake.

textbook.1: FAIL (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — core anatomy right (plump cell, central violet nucleus, branching microvilli-fringed ice-blue canaliculi, ~35 packed orange mitochondria, apical opening), but two long thin hollow tube projections sprout from the upper flanks and read as ducts/flagella (parietal cells have none), and the basal lamina is a cream stripe floating detached below the cell with a clear gap. Fix-prompt: one smooth continuous closed silhouette with the single apical mouth as the only opening; base sits directly on a full-width basal-lamina strip; neighbours as flat soft wedges pressed on the upper flanks.
textbook.2: FAIL (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — the tube projections are gone and the base now touches the lamina, but the artwork is rendered as an inset sheet: a continuous white border/frame ~120 px wide surrounds the charcoal panel on all four sides (measured in the corner pixels), which is the hard framing failure. Fix: escalate to gemini-3-pro-image with the backdrop described as the image itself, reaching all four edges and corners.
textbook.3: PASS (gemini-3-pro-image) — charcoal background reaches all four edges and corners (corner pixels sampled: charcoal, no border). One closed plump pear silhouette; quarter cutaway; central round blue-violet nucleus; branching ice-blue canaliculus fringed with regular microvilli that wraps the nucleus and exits through the single apical mouth (magnified apex crop: clean, microvilli tufts, no text); I count 28 orange-red mitochondria with simple curved cristae arcs packing the cytoplasm; pale yellow-green tubulovesicles scattered near the canal; two cream neighbour wedges on the upper flanks; full-width cream basal-lamina strip under the base (touching at the centre, hairline gap at the flanks, strip ends slightly inset from the frame edges — accepted compromise). Magnified crops of mitochondria zone and apex show cristae read as arcs, not letters; no baked-in text anywhere.

sem.1: PARTIAL (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — subject cell itself is strong (pear-shaped fractured cell, branching microvilli-shaggy canaliculi, fracture face crammed with rounded mitochondria grains), but the surrounding substrate is littered with pale grey rod-shaped debris that reads as bacilli lying around the gland (magnified bottom-left crop), a real mislead next to an H. pylori-adjacent subject. Fix-prompt: the exposed fracture floor around the gland is smooth, bare and featureless.
sem.2: PASS (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — bacteria-like substrate rods are gone; the fracture floor is smooth bare grey. Fractured pear-shaped cell fills the frame; two deep branching canaliculi systems lined with dense white microvilli fur run through the cytoplasm; the fracture face between them is packed wall-to-wall with rounded orange mitochondria grains (hundreds — visually dominating, consistent with ~1/3 volume); pink cell rim, neighbouring fractured cells at the corners, black background top-right reaching the edges, no border. Magnified top and left crops: no lettering; one small raspberry-textured spherical inclusion mid-left (~40 px) of ambiguous identity — accepted, plausible as a fractured organelle. The apical gland-lumen opening is only subtly indicated at the top — accepted compromise; SEM shows surfaces only.

3d.1: FAIL (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — natural tints, packed red bean mitochondria, glossy microvilli-fringed blue canaliculus and central violet nucleus all good, but the basal lamina is a detached white rod floating below the cell with a visible gap (magnified bottom crop), and the yellow-green tubulovesicles are lined up along the cell's outer rim instead of near the canaliculus. Fix-prompt: base rests directly on a full-width basal-lamina band touching the whole underside; tubulovesicles gathered in tight clusters directly alongside the canalicular channels.
3d.2: PASS (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — pale basal-lamina band now spans the full frame width and the cell base sits on it (touching at centre, hairline shadow at the flanks — accepted). Plump triangular-rounded cell on dark seamless background reaching all edges; central violet nucleus; glossy translucent blue canaliculus loops around it with dense fine microvilli fringes and branching tips, opening through the narrow apex at top; I count ~45 packed glossy red-orange bean mitochondria; yellow-green tubulovesicle clusters now hug the canal walls (6 clusters counted along the channel). Magnified centre crop: no text, no letters. Accepted compromise: the tubulovesicle clusters read as grape-like clumps that could be misread as bacterial microcolonies at a glance, though colour and position match the legend.

watercolor.1: PASS (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — warm aged paper fills the entire frame edge-to-edge and corner-to-corner (corner crops: paper texture with faint neighbour-gland pencil sketches, no mat/sheet/frame); teardrop cell with fine ink outlines and soft washes; branching pale ice-blue canaliculi trees fringed with fine ink microvilli strokes on both sides of a central blue-washed nucleus, converging on the apical neck at top; dense red-orange mitochondria ovals (I count ~70, concentrated basally); two ochre tubulovesicle dot-clusters beside the canal trees; a single thin horizontal ink ground-line under the cell reads as the basal lamina in classic atlas style, not as a frame (it spans the width at y≈940 with open paper below). Magnified top-left and bottom crops: the faint sketch circles contain radial hatching only, no lettering; no text anywhere.

reference: PASS — Wikimedia Commons "Parietal cells.jpg" (Public domain, Jpogi at English Wikipedia): genuine H&E light photomicrograph of gastric mucosa with multiple large plump strongly eosinophilic (bright pink) cells with central round nuclei bulging from the gland walls — the diagnostic parietal-cell appearance — among columnar mucous cells. Group composition, but individual parietal cells and their central nuclei are clearly readable. The downloaded frame carried a black slide-pointer marker in the bottom-right corner (bbox x 855–941, y 913–1079); removed by a plain deterministic crop (top-left 900×900, upscaled 1.2× LANCZOS to 1080²; pixel-scan confirms zero near-black pixels remain) — no AI edit, nothing re-illustrated; original kept as real-01 for provenance, cropped real-02 used for display. Web-resolution source (1077×808), so intracellular ultrastructure (canaliculi, mitochondria) is not resolvable in the reference; those structures are labelled only on the illustrated styles.
decision: use attempt 3 (gemini-3-pro-image, escalated after 2 flash fails: tube-projection artifacts, then a white frame); correct closed silhouette, canaliculus-around-nucleus architecture, packed mitochondria; minor accepted compromises: lamina strip slightly inset, hairline base gap at the flanks

use attempt 2; smooth bare substrate (attempt 1 had bacteria-like debris rods), mitochondria-crammed fracture face, microvilli-lined canaliculi; apical opening only subtly visible — surface-only medium, accepted

use attempt 2; attached full-width basal lamina, canal-hugging tubulovesicles (attempt 1 had a floating lamina rod and rim-lined vesicles); natural tints, ~45 packed mitochondria; tubulovesicle clusters read slightly grape-like — accepted
use attempt 1; full-bleed aged paper, correct branching canaliculi + central nucleus + dense mitochondria, atlas-style ground line as basal lamina — no frame
